questions.prompt: Your service sends a request to a payments node and hears nothing back within its timeout. What do you actually know?
options: The payments node has crashed
The request was lost in the network
Nothing for certain: the request or the response may be lost or delayed, or the node may be slow, paused, or down
The payment wasn't processed, so it's safe to retry with a new charge

questions.prompt: You want to measure how long a database query took on one server. Which clock should you use?
options: The time-of-day clock, because it's synchronized with NTP
A monotonic clock, because it never jumps backward
Either one; they're the same on a single machine
Neither; durations can't be measured reliably

questions.prompt: Two replicas resolve conflicts with last write wins using their own time-of-day clocks. Node A's clock runs 50 ms fast. What can happen?
options: Nothing; NTP keeps clocks exactly in sync
A's writes are rejected because their timestamps are in the future
A write from A can beat a later write from B, and B's write is silently discarded
Both writes are kept as siblings

questions.prompt: A worker checks its lease ("10 seconds left"), then hits a 15-second garbage collection pause before writing. What's the danger?
options: None; garbage collection never pauses threads for that long
The lease expired during the pause, another worker took over, and this worker writes anyway, believing it still holds the lease
The write is automatically cancelled by the runtime
The lock service extends the lease while the worker is paused

questions.prompt: A three-node cluster is split by a partition: node A alone on one side, B and C on the other. A was the leader. What should happen?
options: A remains leader because it was elected first
Both sides elect leaders and merge their data afterward
B and C, a majority, may elect a new leader; A must stop acting as leader because it can't reach a quorum
The whole cluster must stop until the partition heals

questions.prompt: What does a fencing token protect against?
options: A client whose lease has expired, perhaps without it knowing, writing to storage after a newer lease holder
Network packets being reordered
Clock drift between data centers
Two clients reading the same row

questions.prompt: Storage has accepted a write with fencing token 34. A write arrives with token 33. What should storage do?
options: Accept it; token 33 was valid once
Reject it: a newer lease holder has already written
Accept it only if it arrives within the lease duration
Ask the lock service whether 33 is still valid

questions.prompt: Why does making a timeout very short to detect failures quickly often backfire?
options: Short timeouts use more CPU
A slow but live node gets declared dead, and failing it over adds load that can make other nodes slow too: a cascade
Timeouts shorter than one second aren't supported by TCP
It doesn't backfire; shorter is always better
